cases.sentence: При слове три Пьер ___ пошел вперед, сбиваясь с протоптанной дорожки и шагая по цельному снегу.
cases.explain: «быстрыми шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “So I can fire when I like!” said Pierre, and at the word “three,” he went quickly forward, missing the trodden path and stepping into the deep snow. He held the pistol in his right hand at arm’s length, apparently afraid of shooting himself with it. His left hand he held carefully back, because he wished to support his right hand with it and knew he must not do so. Having advanced six paces and strayed off the track into the snow, Pierre looked down at his feet, then quickly glanced at Dólokhov and, bending his finger as he had been shown, fired. Not at all expecting so loud a report, Pierre shuddered at the sound and then, smiling at his own sensations, stood still. The smoke, rendered denser by the mist, prevented him from seeing anything for an instant, but there was no second report as he had expected. He only heard Dólokhov’s hurried steps, and his figure came in view through the smoke. He was pressing one hand to his left side, while the other clutched his drooping pistol. His face was pale. Rostóv ran toward him and said something.

cases.sentence: — Не... нет, — проговорил сквозь зубы Долохов, — нет, не кончено, — и сделав еще несколько падающих, ковыляющих шагов до ___, упал на снег подле нее.
cases.explain: «самой сабли» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “No-o-o!” muttered Dólokhov through his teeth, “no, it’s not over.” And after stumbling a few staggering steps right up to the saber, he sank on the snow beside it. His left hand was bloody; he wiped it on his coat and supported himself with it. His frowning face was pallid and quivered. “Plea …” began Dólokhov, but could not at first pronounce the word.

cases.sentence: В одно и то же время они услыхали выстрел и ___ Долохова.
cases.explain: «злой крик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Pierre, with a gentle smile of pity and remorse, his arms and legs helplessly spread out, stood with his broad chest directly facing Dólokhov and looked sorrowfully at him. Denísov, Rostóv, and Nesvítski closed their eyes. At the same instant they heard a report and Dólokhov’s angry cry.

cases.sentence: Ростов поехал вперед исполнять поручение, и к великому удивлению своему узнал, что Долохов, этот буян, бретёр-Долохов жил в Москве с старушкой-матерью и горбатою сестрой, и был самый ___ и брат.
cases.explain: «нежный сын» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Rostóv went on ahead to do what was asked, and to his great surprise learned that Dólokhov the brawler, Dólokhov the bully, lived in Moscow with an old mother and a hunchback sister, and was the most affectionate of sons and brothers.
